steps.text: The wrist is rotating, but I still need a clear view of the knob to confirm that it followed. I’m completing this small turn, then releasing and lifting the gripper to inspect it.
The pan’s overhang appears to be obstructing the approach from above. I’m withdrawing toward the front of the stove and changing to a side approach to give the gripper more clearance.
The side approach is close to the arm’s joint limits. I’m adjusting the base and wrist position so the fingers can reach the knob without straining against those limits.
The gripper is meeting resistance near the front lip of the stove. I’m tilting the wrist downward slightly to keep the palm above the lip while the fingertips approach the knob.
The base has moved back about 20 cm, giving the arm more room to extend. I’m now approaching the knob again with the wrist tilted to clear the stove’s front edge.

The camera evidence shows the leftmost knob rotated about 40° from its initial position, and blue flame is visible beneath the pan on the front-left burner. The gripper is open and clear of the knob. I’m stopping control commands to preserve that state.
